IPC4 Host-DSP Protocol API#

The IPC4 protocol defines the structured binary communication interface between the host operating system driver and the Sound Open Firmware (SOF) DSP runtime. Used extensively across modern Intel platforms (Tiger Lake, Alder Lake, Raptor Lake, Meteor Lake, Arrow Lake, Lunar Lake, and Panther Lake), IPC4 governs audio pipeline construction, dynamic module lifecycle, inter-module pin binding, hardware peripheral gateway configuration, large parameter configuration handshakes, and real-time asynchronous telemetry.

Architecture & Protocol Overview#

The IPC4 protocol is built upon hardware doorbells, shared SRAM mailbox windows, and a uniform 64-bit message envelope.

1. Shared Memory Mailbox Windows#

Host and DSP exchange control messages and telemetry through memory-mapped SRAM windows:

  • Mailbox Window 0 (Control & Status):

    • Offset 0x0000 - 0x0FFF (Firmware Status & Telemetry Registers): Exposes the 32-bit Firmware Status Register (fsr), Last Error Code (lec), Power Status (fps), ROM information, pipeline LPIB positions, real-time PeakVol meters, and Link Linear Position (LLP) wallclock readings (ipc4_fw_registers).

    • Offset 0x1000 - 0x1FFF (Downlink Mailbox): Host writes request payloads (e.g. module initialization blobs, pipeline configs).

    • Offset 0x2000 - 0x2FFF (Uplink Mailbox): DSP writes reply payloads and unsolicited asynchronous notification structures.

  • Mailbox Window 1 (Probes & Bulk Data): Dedicated memory window for audio extraction/injection probes, trace DMA streams, and bulk configuration buffers.

2. 64-bit Message Envelope#

Every IPC4 communication consists of two 32-bit hardware registers: the Primary Register and the Extension Register.

+-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
|                                  IPC4 Primary Header (DWORD 0)                                |
+---------------+---------+--------+--------------------+---------------------------------------+
| Bit 31 (RSVD) | 30 (TGT)| 29(RSP)| Bits 28:24 (TYPE)  | Bits 23:0 (Type-Specific Parameters)  |
+---------------+---------+--------+--------------------+---------------------------------------+
| Reserved (0)  | 0=GLB   | 0=REQ  | Opcode (0..31)     | Module Instance / Pipeline ID /       |
|               | 1=MOD   | 1=RSP  |                    | Status Code (in replies)              |
+---------------+---------+--------+--------------------+---------------------------------------+

+-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
|                                 IPC4 Extension Header (DWORD 1)                               |
+---------------------------------------+---------------+---------------------------------------+
| Bits 31:30 (Reserved)                 | Bit 29..24    | Bits 23:0 (Extension-Specific Data)   |
+---------------------------------------+---------------+---------------------------------------+
| Reserved bits                         | Large Config  | Param ID / Data Offset & Size /       |
|                                       | Flags (FB/LB) | Pipeline Context Pages                |
+---------------------------------------+---------------+---------------------------------------+

  • Target Bit (``msg_tgt``):

    • 0 (Global Message): Targets firmware core services (pipelines, base firmware, gateway control).

    • 1 (Module Message): Addressed to a specific module instance identified by its 16-bit Module ID and 8-bit Instance ID.

  • Response Bit (``rsp``):

    • 0: Request from sender (or unsolicited DSP-to-host notification).

    • 1: Reply to a previous request, returning status code in bits 23:0 of Primary.

3. Doorbell Handshake Flow#

Command exchange follows a strict, non-reentrant hardware doorbell handshake:

Host Driver                                                  DSP Firmware
    |                                                              |
    |  1. Write payload to Downlink Mailbox (Window 0)             |
    |  2. Write Primary & Extension registers                      |
    |  3. Set Host-to-DSP Doorbell (BUSY = 1)                      |
    |------------------------------------------------------------->|  (Interrupt)
    |                                                              |
    |                                                              |  4. Read Primary & Ext
    |                                                              |  5. Dispatch command
    |                                                              |  6. Write reply payload
    |                                                              |     to Uplink Mailbox
    |                                                              |  7. Write status to Primary
    |                                                              |  8. Clear DSP BUSY &
    |  (Interrupt)                                                 |     Set DSP-to-Host DONE
    |<-------------------------------------------------------------|
    |                                                              |
    |  9. Read reply status and Uplink payload                     |
    | 10. Clear DONE bit (handshake complete)                      |
    |                                                              |

4. Audio Pipeline Construction & State Machine#

Audio processing graphs are built and controlled dynamically by the host driver:

Host Driver                                                  DSP Firmware
    |                                                              |
    |  SOF_IPC4_GLB_CREATE_PIPELINE (ppl_id, priority, memory)     |
    |------------------------------------------------------------->|  Create pipeline container
    |<-------------------------------------------------------------|  Reply (STATUS_SUCCESS)
    |                                                              |
    |  SOF_IPC4_MOD_INIT_INSTANCE (mod_id, inst_id, base_cfg)      |
    |------------------------------------------------------------->|  Instantiate module in pipeline
    |<-------------------------------------------------------------|  Reply (STATUS_SUCCESS)
    |                                                              |
    |  SOF_IPC4_MOD_BIND (src_mod, src_pin -> dst_mod, dst_pin)    |
    |------------------------------------------------------------->|  Connect inter-module queue
    |<-------------------------------------------------------------|  Reply (STATUS_SUCCESS)
    |                                                              |
    |  SOF_IPC4_GLB_SET_PIPELINE_STATE (PAUSED)                    |
    |------------------------------------------------------------->|  Allocate buffers & gateways
    |<-------------------------------------------------------------|  Reply (STATUS_SUCCESS)
    |                                                              |
    |  SOF_IPC4_GLB_SET_PIPELINE_STATE (RUNNING)                   |
    |------------------------------------------------------------->|  Start processing tasks (LL/DP)
    |<-------------------------------------------------------------|  Reply (STATUS_SUCCESS)
    |                                                              |

State transitions adhere to strict ordering:

  • Forward Transitions (RESET -> PAUSED -> RUNNING): Processed from source modules to sink modules.

  • Reverse Transitions (RUNNING -> PAUSED -> RESET): Processed in strict reverse order (sink modules to source modules) to guarantee clean drain without FIFO underflow.

5. Large Configuration Multi-Chunk Protocol#

When parameter data exceeds the mailbox capacity (4KB), the IPC4 protocol utilizes fragmented multi-chunk transactions:

Host Driver                                                  DSP Firmware
    |                                                              |
    |  LARGE_CONFIG_SET (Chunk 0, first_block=1, last_block=0)     |
    |  [Payload: bytes 0 .. 4095]                                  |
    |------------------------------------------------------------->|  Accumulate into staging buffer
    |<-------------------------------------------------------------|  Reply (STATUS_SUCCESS)
    |                                                              |
    |  LARGE_CONFIG_SET (Chunk 1, first_block=0, last_block=0)     |
    |  [Payload: bytes 4096 .. 8191]                               |
    |------------------------------------------------------------->|  Accumulate
    |<-------------------------------------------------------------|  Reply (STATUS_SUCCESS)
    |                                                              |
    |  LARGE_CONFIG_SET (Chunk 2, first_block=0, last_block=1)     |
    |  [Payload: final bytes]                                      |
    |------------------------------------------------------------->|  Commit full parameter blob
    |<-------------------------------------------------------------|  Reply (STATUS_SUCCESS)
    |                                                              |

Protocol API Subsystems#

The IPC4 API reference is organized into eight specialized functional subsystems:

1. Message Envelope & Protocol Handlers#

Defines the fundamental 64-bit message envelope, primary and extension register formats, global opcodes, status codes, and host-DSP message routing bridges.

group IPC4 Message Envelope & Dispatch

64-bit mailbox message envelope formats, primary/extension registers, command target routing, reply status, and compound message barriers.

enum ipc4_status#

IPC4 host-DSP status and error codes.

Returned in the lower 24 bits of the Primary reply DWORD (ipc4_message_reply::primary::r::status). Standard status codes are common across global and module commands, while values >= 100 convey subsystem-specific failures (module management, probes, gateways, and clocking).

struct ipc_cmd_hdr#
#include <src/include/ipc3/header.h>

Generic message header.

Generic raw 64-bit IPC4 message header registers.

IPC MAJOR 3 version. All IPC3 messages use this header as abstraction to platform specific calls.

All IPC4 messages are passed across the mailbox as a pair of 32-bit registers (Primary DWORD + Extension DWORD).

uint32_t pri#

Primary 32-bit register value.

Extension 32-bit register value.

struct ipc4_message_reply#
#include <src/include/ipc4/header.h>

Standard 64-bit IPC4 message reply envelope.

Written to the mailbox registers by the DSP firmware upon command completion. The primary register contains the processing status code in its lower 24 bits.

uint32_t msg_tgt#

Target: symmetric to request (FW_GEN_MSG or MODULE_MSG).

Hardware control reserved bit.

2. Audio Formats, Pins & Stream Descriptors#

Defines the binary serialization format for multi-channel audio streams, PCM sample representations, container bit depths, channel maps, and dynamic input/output pin formats.

Note

Sample type enumeration entries (such as IPC4_TYPE_MSB_INTEGER vs IPC4_TYPE_LSB_INTEGER) describe valid audio bit alignment within the sample container memory word (e.g. S24 valid bits aligned at bits [31:8] vs [23:0]) rather than byte endianness, remaining little-endian.

group IPC4 Audio Formats & Pin Contracts

Audio format specification bitfields, sampling rates, bit depths, channel configurations, and pin format descriptors.

struct ipc4_cfg_param_id_data f#

3. Dynamic Modules & Configuration Handshake#

Governs audio module instantiation, deletion, dynamic binding/unbinding of module pins, D0ix power state switching, and small/large parameter configuration transactions. Target DSP core affinity (core_id) is platform-dependent, ranging from 0 up to CONFIG_CORE_COUNT - 1.

group IPC4 Module Architecture & Dynamic Binding

Module instantiation, dynamic queue/pin binding, small/large parameter configuration handshake, and module power transitions.

4. Audio Pipelines & Scheduling Priorities#

Covers audio pipeline graph allocation, scheduling domain priorities (Low Latency vs Data Processing), pipeline state transitions (Reset, Paused, Running), memory context queries, and direct DMA chaining.

struct ipc4_pipeline_set_state_data#
#include <src/include/ipc4/pipeline.h>

Payload array containing pipeline IDs for multi-pipeline state transitions.

Host SW sends this message to set a pipeline to the specified state.

If there are multiple pipelines, from FW input to FW output, connected in a data processing stream, the driver should start them in reverse order, beginning with pipeline connected to the output gateway, in order to avoid overruns (FW protects the output gateway against underruns in this scenario).

If driver starts multiple pipelines using a single Set Pipeline State command, it should take care of the pipeline ID order in the command payload to follow the above rule.

sync_stop_start indicates whether all specified pipelines’ gateways should be started with a minimal delay possible. If this flag is set to 0 while multiple pipelines are specified, the target pipelines’ state is adjusted pipeline by pipeline meaning that internal propagation to all child modules may take more time between reaching state of attached gateways. Output and input gateways are grouped separately, and started/stopped separately.

NOTE: Task Creation/Registration is part of the first state transition. There is no other dedicated call for this.

struct ipc4_pipeline_set_state#
#include <src/include/ipc4/pipeline.h>

Pipeline state transition command structure (SOF_IPC4_GLB_SET_PIPELINE_STATE).

6. Hardware Gateways & Peripherals#

Encodes hardware connector addressing (node IDs) and configuration blobs for Intel High Definition Audio (HDA), Audio Hub Link (ALH / SoundWire) aggregation, Digital Microphones (DMIC), and Synchronous Serial Ports (SSP / I2S).

group IPC4 Hardware Audio Gateways

Audio gateway addressing (HD-Audio host/link, SoundWire ALH aggregation, DMIC link, SSP/I2S), gateway attributes, and NHLT configuration blobs.

7. Asynchronous Notifications & Mailbox Registers#

Details unsolicited DSP-to-host event notifications (underrun/overrun alarms, budget violations, voice activity wake words), and Mailbox Window 0 telemetry register layouts. Unsolicited notifications use opcode SOF_IPC4_GLB_NOTIFICATION (opcode 27 / 0x1B). Notification dispatch functions return true when the notification is either queued or suppressed by the notification mask, and false if the notification pool is temporarily exhausted, indicating that the caller should retry.

group IPC4 Asynchronous Notifications & Telemetry Registers

Unsolicited DSP-to-host notifications, resource event reports, keyword detection events, watchdog alerts, and Mailbox Window 0 status registers.

8. Telemetry, Probes & Logging#

Covers real-time host audio probe injection and extraction points, DMA probe streams, trace logging configuration, and mtrace memory buffers. Callers specify the DMA stream tag for injection probe points, whereas for extraction probes firmware automatically binds the probe point to the active extraction DMA channel.

group IPC4 Telemetry, Logging & Audio Probes

Host DMA trace logging control, audio probe injection and extraction data streams, and module-specific configuration payloads.
